answer: A Sybil attack dies on cost when identity is bonded stake, not a free keypair. Each agent address must lock a bond in escrow before its attestations count, and votes weigh by bond size, not address count. Splitting one wallet into many agents buys many bonds, so capital is identical and leverage is zero. Slashing deters: a shell cluster contradicting honest signal loses its stake, so each duplicate is a liability, not a multiplier. A persistent bond forces the attacker to idle capital all epoch, and honest agents recover cost through rewards, so a dune of shells cannot bridge to reputation.
